titles.title: Tears of Steel
titles.tagline: Save the world. Fix the past.
titles.synopsis: In a future Amsterdam overrun by robots, a group of warriors and scientists stage a desperate gamble: recreate the moment a young scientist broke up with the man who would go on to build the machines. A live-action sci-fi short with Blender-made visual effects.

stream.note: This demo stream burns the current bitrate into the top-left corner, so you can watch adaptive quality switching happen.

titles.title: Sintel
titles.tagline: A lonely search for a lost friend.
titles.synopsis: A young woman named Sintel crosses deserts, snowfields and a vast walled city searching for Scales, the baby dragon she once rescued and raised. The Blender Foundation's third open movie.

stream.note: AES-128 encrypted HLS: the player fetches the key and decrypts each segment.

titles.title: Big Buck Bunny
titles.tagline: Never mess with a big, gentle bunny.
titles.synopsis: A giant, good-natured rabbit just wants to enjoy a sunny morning in the meadow. Three rodent bullies have other plans, and they're about to learn that even the gentlest bunny has his limits.

titles.title: Elephants Dream
titles.tagline: The machine is only what you believe it is.
titles.synopsis: Emo and Proog wander an endless, shifting machine that Proog believes he understands completely, until Emo starts to see it differently. The world's first open movie, made entirely with open-source tools.

stream.note: Progressive file, not HLS, so it plays at one fixed quality (720p).

titles.title: Shark Dive 360°
titles.synopsis: A 360° dive among sharks off the ocean floor. It's here as the app's 4K showcase: the adaptive ladder goes from 480p all the way to 3840×2048. The footage is equirectangular VR, so it looks stretched in a flat player.

stream.note: Public 4K HLS test stream. Premium unlocks the 2160p rendition.
